exercises.q: I'll knock all your teeth out.
exercises.why: **выбью** — вы́бить (perfective): to beat out, to knock out, to dislodge. Wiktionary: вы́- + бить.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **сбивал** — сбива́ть (imperfective): to knock down, to shake down, to cause to fall; to knock down, to beat down; to put out; to tread down. Wiktionary: сбить + -вать.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **сбивай** — сбива́ть (imperfective): to knock down, to shake down, to cause to fall; to knock down, to beat down; to put out; to tread down. Wiktionary: сбить + -вать.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **избил** — изби́ть (perfective): to beat, to thrash (unmercifully). Wiktionary: из- + бить.

exercises.q: They fixed the sign to the wall.
exercises.why: **прибили** — приби́ть (perfective): to nail down (to attach with a nail); to move, to drive somewhere (of the wind or water); to press to the ground (by an impact or by wind or water); (colloquial) to kill. Wiktionary: при- + бить.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Nail the notice on the trunk of that tree.
exercises.why: **Прибейте** — приби́ть (perfective): to nail down (to attach with a nail); to move, to drive somewhere (of the wind or water); to press to the ground (by an impact or by wind or water); (colloquial) to kill. Wiktionary: при- + бить.

exercises.q: He loaded his stomach with food.
exercises.why: **набил** — наби́ть (perfective): to stuff, to pack, to fill; to fix (onto); (colloquial) to type (some text); to break, to smash (a lot of something). Wiktionary: на- + бить.
